clusters.name: Formula written into an answer cell instead of a literal value
clusters.root_cause: Primary metric hard_no_recalc: evaluation.py::compare_workbooks loads the produced file with openpyxl.load_workbook(data_only=True) and REWARD_RECALC defaults to 0, so nothing recalculates. openpyxl saves a formula with no cached <v>, so the graded cell reads back None. Most instructions literally ask for a formula ('I need a formula...', 'use INDEX/MATCH', 'adapt this macro'), so the agent complied correctly and scored 0.

sub_cases.name: formula already present in the answer cell
sub_cases.note: pre-existing formulas also lose their cached value on save, so leaving or text-editing them is equally fatal

sub_cases.name: reported as 'Excel error text (e.g. #N/A)'
sub_cases.note: same cluster seen through the recalculated diagnostic copy. None wrote an '#N/A' literal and none used data_only=True; they wrote post-2007 functions bare (AGGREGATE, UNIQUE, TEXTJOIN, FILTER, TEXTSPLIT, MAXIFS) which the xlsx grammar requires as _xlfn.*, so LibreOffice resolved them to #NAME?/#VALUE!. Verified against the saved artifacts by a subagent.

clusters.name: Blanket-overwriting the whole answer_position rectangle
clusters.root_cause: answer_position is the CHECKED range, not a box to fill. Cells already holding the right value are typically the user's hand-done worked example (48588: B2:B18 pre-filled and correct, agent overwrote all 42 cells), and cells whose answer is genuinely blank must stay blank (50768: 6 of 9 matrix boxes).

clusters.name: No verification and no inspection - effectively single-shot
clusters.root_cause: The adapter's built-in template said 'once that file exists, you are done'. Median 3 of 30 rounds used; 59196 and 51-12 did zero inspection rounds. 3 of the 4 non-formula failures had the ground truth sitting in the sheet (59196 H3='D'; 43436 header text + neighbouring example formula; 51-12 row-2 markers) and none were read.

clusters.name: Right answer, wrong Python type
clusters.root_cause: transform_value rounds numbers to 2dp and coerces numeric-looking strings, then compare_cell_value rejects on type(v1) != type(v2). Text written as a number, or a date written as a string, fails. All 6 are also cluster A, so A's fix is a precondition for D being observable.

clusters.name: Loose prose outranked by the in-sheet specification
clusters.root_cause: 43436 counted records open DURING the month although the column header says 'Open by of end of May 2022' and the user's own neighbouring example formula H2=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"") spells out the end-of-period reading; all 5 cells came out uniformly high. 59196 anchored INDEX($D$1:$G$1,...) on an empty row 1 because the pandas preview returned all-Unnamed columns - the real headers are in row 2.

clusters.name: Float threshold comparison overshoot
clusters.root_cause: value >= ref * 1.10 misses exact 10% steps because 100 * 1.10 == 110.00000000000001; the agent counted 2 where golden is 4. Only pure-computation failure in the set.

clusters.name: Formula written into an answer cell instead of a literal value
clusters.root_cause: Primary metric hard_no_recalc: evaluation.py::compare_workbooks loads the produced file with openpyxl.load_workbook(data_only=True) and REWARD_RECALC defaults to 0, so nothing recalculates. openpyxl saves a formula with no cached <v>, so the graded cell reads back None. Most instructions literally ask for a formula ('I need a formula...', 'use INDEX/MATCH', 'adapt this macro'), so the agent complied correctly and scored 0.

sub_cases.name: formula already present in the answer cell
sub_cases.note: pre-existing formulas also lose their cached value on save, so leaving or text-editing them is equally fatal

sub_cases.name: reported as 'Excel error text (e.g. #N/A)'
sub_cases.note: same cluster seen through the recalculated diagnostic copy. None wrote an '#N/A' literal and none used data_only=True; they wrote post-2007 functions bare (AGGREGATE, UNIQUE, TEXTJOIN, FILTER, TEXTSPLIT, MAXIFS) which the xlsx grammar requires as _xlfn.*, so LibreOffice resolved them to #NAME?/#VALUE!. Verified against the saved artifacts by a subagent.

clusters.name: Blanket-overwriting the whole answer_position rectangle
clusters.root_cause: answer_position is the CHECKED range, not a box to fill. Cells already holding the right value are typically the user's hand-done worked example (48588: B2:B18 pre-filled and correct, agent overwrote all 42 cells), and cells whose answer is genuinely blank must stay blank (50768: 6 of 9 matrix boxes).

clusters.name: No verification and no inspection - effectively single-shot
clusters.root_cause: The adapter's built-in template said 'once that file exists, you are done'. Median 3 of 30 rounds used; 59196 and 51-12 did zero inspection rounds. 3 of the 4 non-formula failures had the ground truth sitting in the sheet (59196 H3='D'; 43436 header text + neighbouring example formula; 51-12 row-2 markers) and none were read.

clusters.name: Right answer, wrong Python type
clusters.root_cause: transform_value rounds numbers to 2dp and coerces numeric-looking strings, then compare_cell_value rejects on type(v1) != type(v2). Text written as a number, or a date written as a string, fails. All 6 are also cluster A, so A's fix is a precondition for D being observable.

clusters.name: Loose prose outranked by the in-sheet specification
clusters.root_cause: 43436 counted records open DURING the month although the column header says 'Open by of end of May 2022' and the user's own neighbouring example formula H2=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"") spells out the end-of-period reading; all 5 cells came out uniformly high. 59196 anchored INDEX($D$1:$G$1,...) on an empty row 1 because the pandas preview returned all-Unnamed columns - the real headers are in row 2.

clusters.name: Float threshold comparison overshoot
clusters.root_cause: value >= ref * 1.10 misses exact 10% steps because 100 * 1.10 == 110.00000000000001; the agent counted 2 where golden is 4. Only pure-computation failure in the set.

# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — created both capability files from an EMPTY seed; the headline fact is that a formula in a graded cell always scores 0

The seed was a true no-skill control: `prompt.md` was 0 bytes, so `_read_system_prompt` returned
`""` and **no system message was sent at all**, and `task_template.md` was absent, so the adapter's
built-in `_TASK_TEMPLATE` was used — which contains *"once that file exists, you are done"* and no
verification step. So this iteration is a creation, not an edit.

- **Changes I made**
  - `prompt.md` (created, 129 lines) — Rule 1 *answer cells hold literal values, never formulas*,
    with the mechanism (cluster A, 25/26 failures); Rule 1.2–1.3 *a pre-existing formula in an answer
    cell can't stand either; recover its value with a second `data_only=True` load* (cluster A-sub);
    Rule 2 *write the right Python type*, as a 4-row table off the scorer (cluster D); Rule 3
    *`answer_position` is CHECKED, not a box to fill* (cluster B); Rule 4 *sheet resolution:
    `sheetnames[0]`, not `wb.active`*; Rule 5 *don't write the output with pandas; openpyxl or
    `zipfile` XML*; working-style section — in-sheet header/example outranks loose prose (cluster E),
    integer-scaled percentage thresholds (cluster F), the `max_row` auto-vivification trap, never
    re-run a failing block unchanged.
  - `task_template.md` (created) — restructured the contract into **READ → SOLVE → CHECK** with the
    `{max_turns}` budget made usable (cluster C, all 26); **deleted** the "file exists ⇒ done" line
    and replaced it with "you are done when the Round-3 output is all-clear"; field-semantics section
    including the pandas-preview offset (`preview row i == Excel row i+2`) and the all-`Unnamed:`
    header-row warning (cluster E); the two-load `ws`/`wsv` idiom; and a copyable Round-3 check that
    **asserts no cell in the range holds a formula** and diffs the range against the input.
  - All 6 required placeholders + `{max_turns}` intact, 0 unknown placeholders, template renders,
    all 4 embedded python blocks compile. No task id, value, date or answer appears anywhere.

- **Expected effect + why it's safe, per change**
  - Rule 1 should move cluster A (25 tasks) — every one of them wrote a correct formula into the
    graded range and read back `None`. Safe because **0 of the 14 passing tasks write a formula as
    their graded answer**; 6698 writes a formula *plus* a hand-patched cached value, and the integer
    Rule 1 has it write is the same number it patched in, so graded content is unchanged.
  - Rule 2's type table should pick up cluster D (6 tasks) once A unblocks them. The "normalise only
    the comparison, write back the original value" clause is there so 463-17 and 416-15 don't change;
    the formatting sentence is deliberately soft so 560-12 / 6698 / 80-42 still do the explicit
    formatting work they pass with.
  - Rule 3 should move cluster B (5 tasks). Two carve-outs make it safe: *match an absence convention
    the neighbouring rows already use* (without it, **80-42 breaks deterministically** — it passes
    only because it writes literal `"None"`/`"N/A"` across ~7000 cells), and *clearing is right when
    the instruction's uniformly-applied rule covers the cell* (**382-10** must clear `A18`'s stale
    `=IFERROR(#REF!/#REF!,0)` to `None`, and the instruction never names A18).
  - Rule 5 bans only the pandas writers and explicitly permits `zipfile`/XML surgery, because
    **463-17 and 6698 both pass that way** (463-17 after its openpyxl attempt timed out).
  - The Round-3 check is the structural fix for cluster C: verification is now the *definition* of
    done rather than advice, and the `assert` makes cluster A mechanically impossible to miss. Its
    enumeration is clipped to `chk.max_row` because 80-42's range is `A2:L8000` = 95,988 cells and
    the unclipped version risked the 60-second block limit on a **passing** task (clipped: 12,012).
  - Turn budget is not a risk: the largest number of rounds any trace used was 6 of 30.

- **Building on prior RESULTS** — none exist. This is iteration 1: `LEDGER.md` and `RUNMAP.md` are
  empty, `prior_iterations/` has no entries, and there is no `rejected.jsonl` to avoid. I did read
  the repo's prior *experiment* champion for this benchmark
  (`docs/experiments/2026-09-26-...-gemma-4-31b/champion/task_template.md`) as reference; it
  confirms the ordered READ/SOLVE/CHECK shape, but I did not copy it — it never states that the
  grader does **not recalculate** (the fact that decides 25 of my 26 failures), and three of its
  rules are the exact blunt phrasings my passing-trace audit flagged as regressions here.

- **Refuted hypotheses** — nothing is refuted by a RESULT yet. Two of my own hypotheses were refuted
  by evidence during this iteration and should not be re-tested: (1) the six *"Excel error text
  (e.g. #N/A)"* tasks are **not** a separate cluster and are **not** caused by `data_only=True`
  round-tripping or by agent-written `"#N/A"` literals — no trace used `data_only=True` and none
  wrote such a literal; they are cluster A seen through the recalculated diagnostic copy, where bare
  post-2007 functions (`AGGREGATE`, `UNIQUE`, `TEXTJOIN`, `FILTER`, `TEXTSPLIT`, `MAXIFS`) resolve to
  `#NAME?` because the xlsx grammar requires the `_xlfn.` prefix. (2) There is **no environment
  fault**: the grader behaved consistently on all 40 tasks, and 463-17's 60-second timeout was the
  agent's own `ws[f"A{row}"]` auto-vivification loop, not infrastructure.

- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked** — all six got an edit, so nothing is knowingly left on
  the table; what's untested is whether the *reader* complies. The two tasks I expect to resist are
  43436 and 51-12: they need correct reasoning, not a missing fact, and I shipped only the general
  lesson behind each. 50768 (a 9-box matrix where 6 boxes must stay blank) is the single hardest
  cluster-B case and may need a layout-specific guard if Rule 3 alone doesn't take.

- **Plateau signal** — n/a at iteration 1. The lever used here is the biggest one available:
  content-from-nothing plus one piece of **code enforcement** (the `assert not formulas` in the
  CHECK block) rather than trusting prose, which is what the strong-tier reader guidance asks for.

- **Focus next iteration** — read this candidate's RESULT first. If Rule 1 lands, the remaining
  failures should be clusters B/D/E, and the next lever is tightening the Round-3 check (e.g. making
  the `changed`-set comparison an assert too, or adding a type-expectation line) rather than adding
  more prose. If Rule 1 does **not** land, the question is compliance, not knowledge: move the
  formula ban out of `prompt.md` and into the per-task template next to the write step, where this
  reader is far more likely to act on it. Either way, check the RESULT's `broke={...}` against the
  four at-risk passing tasks named above (80-42, 382-10, 463-17, 6698) before changing their
  carve-outs.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.925 Δ=+0.575 · fixed={12864, 267-18, 2768, 37378, 37456, 39046, 43436, 45635, 46897, 48588, 48620, 48921, 50768, 51-12, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 7902, 8942, 9726} · broke={560-12} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.925 Δ=+0.575 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — all 3 remaining failures self-certified a wrong answer, so the check now compares the saved file against a per-cell verdict record instead of against the agent's own intent

Only 3 tasks fail (59595, 560-12, 9569) and I drove **all three** to root cause. They look like three
different bugs and they are — but they share one defect: the Round-3 check was composed entirely of
*shape* assertions the agent interpreted itself, so each of the three got output consistent with its
own wrong intent and stopped with ~27 of 30 rounds unused. 9 edits, 7 distinct improvement types.

- **Changes I made**
  - `prompt.md` Rule 2 table + new normalisation block (cluster I, *wrong type*) — corrected: off
    `transform_value`, `int` vs `float` **never** matters and neither does a `float()`-parseable
    string, so `42`/`42.0`/`"42"` are one value. Names the type errors that *do* cost cells.
  - `prompt.md` new **Rule 2b** (cluster I, 9569) — *write the value THROUGH; do not round it.* The
    grader rounds to 2 dp itself, so rounding to 3–4 dp first can only create `x.xx5` ties. Plus: a
    pre-filled cell's **decimal count is not part of the specification** — reproduce a worked
    example's *rule*, never its digit count. Plus: tolerances on the data's scale, not `1e-15`.
  - `prompt.md` Rule 3 new first bullet (cluster H, 560-12) — the box's top-left corner is not
    automatically where the answer starts; resolve the anchor first; padding is graded as whatever it
    already contained.
  - `prompt.md` Rule 3 — **replaced** the worked-example bullet (cluster G, 59595). That bullet is my
    own cand_0001 wording and is the *proximate cause* of 59595. Now a 5-row
    `currently holds × rule yields → verdict` table + an explicit ban on `if cell.value is None` as
    the condition that decides which cells get filled.
  - `task_template.md` `answer_position` bullet (cluster H) — 3-step anchor resolution (*named* →
    *described* → else the corner), the three addresses that are **not** the anchor (inside a quoted
    formula / a schematic sketch of column order / the far end of a destination range), and a worked
    12-cell example whose anchor sits one row below the box corner.
  - `task_template.md` Round 1 (clusters G, H) — deleted *"Leave those example cells as they are"*;
    now requires two **printed** conclusions, `ANCHOR:` and `PRE-FILLED:`, with the three-way
    judgement for each pre-filled cell. Round 1 also builds `CELLS` itself.
  - `task_template.md` Round 2 (cluster G) — `PLAN[a1] = value or LEAVE` for **every** graded cell,
    `assert set(PLAN) == set(CELLS)`, verdict printed beside current content, then write only the
    non-`LEAVE` entries. Explicitly *"a decision record, not a mandated mechanism"*.
  - `task_template.md` Round 3 (clusters G, I) — new `assert not offplan`: the saved file must agree
    with `PLAN` cell for cell, via a `same()` helper mirroring the grader's `None`/`""` equivalence.
    Four confirmation points became five; point 5 adds *"agreement that you had to **round** to
    obtain is not agreement"*.
  - `task_template.md` interaction contract — softened the over-strong implication that a green
    assert means done: *"whether `PLAN` is right is a judgement you still have to make"*, and
    shrinking `PLAN` so a disagreeing cell becomes `LEAVE` is the evasion the check cannot catch.
  - All 6 required placeholders + `{max_turns}` intact, 0 unknown, renders (14,964 chars), all 5
    python blocks compile. No task id, value, date or answer appears anywhere.

- **Expected effect + why it's safe, per change**
  - **59595** (13/16 cells right) gated its write `if 12 <= r <= 19`, leaving the owner's `'n/a'` in
    C4/C5/C6 where gold holds `4, 6, 12` — and its own rule run on those rows yields exactly those
    three values. The verdict table + `assert set(PLAN)==set(CELLS)` + `assert not offplan` make
    skipping them impossible; Round 1's `PRE-FILLED` printout is what classifies `'n/a'` as a
    placeholder. Safe: the asserts compare the file against the agent's **own** `PLAN`, so a correct
    complete write cannot trip them.
  - **560-12** (the task cand_0001 broke) is a pure one-row anchor shift: instruction says *"the
    answer should be put from I3"*, agent anchored at the box corner I2. The `int where str expected`
    feedback is a symptom — a count landed in the header row. Anchor precedence + the required
    `ANCHOR:` printout fix it. Safe only because of four audited carve-outs: **2768** (schematic
    sketch names column F, real destination H), **53647** (given range E7:E16, gold E15 **empty**),
    **80-42** and **463-17** (*described* starts, which step 2 resolves where they already resolve).
  - **9569**'s selection rule was **identical to gold**; the defect was a gratuitous
    `round(float(v),4)` adopted to reproduce the owner's hand-typed `AO9 = 0.1707` — which gold
    *overwrites* with `0.170687841`. Rule 2b inverts that inference. Safe: it only fires where the
    agent was about to round *without being told to*.
  - **Blast radius, stated honestly:** d/f/g are **BOUNDED in outcome but WIDE in process** — all 40
    trajectories gain a `PLAN` and two printouts. Outcome should be unchanged because `PLAN` is the
    agent's own intent made explicit. ~21 passing tasks write `int` and the type edit tells the agent
    int/float is *invisible* rather than asking it to convert; **50768**'s `'2'`-as-`str` is protected
    by *"a pre-filled neighbour is the authority"*; **463-17/6698**'s XML path by *"not a mandated
    mechanism"*; **6698** is why check point 5 stays **soft and never an assert** (it passes by
    overwriting a cached figure that was itself wrong).
  - **Snippet execution.** openpyxl is unavailable here, so per `META_INSIGHTS.md` I ran the shipped
    snippets' logic against a faithful `Worksheet.__getitem__`/`range_boundaries` stub on six shapes:
    single cell, the 560-12 geometry, the 59595 geometry, the 95,988-cell range (clips to 47,988 via
    `max_row`, 0.25 s), the `""`↔`None` round-trip (must not fire — doesn't), and a deliberately
    missed cell (`offplan` must fire — does). No branch raises.

- **Building on prior RESULTS** — cand_0001 ACCEPTED, val 0.925, `broke={560-12}`, `fixed={24}`. Two
  things followed from that stamp. (1) `broke={560-12}` is cluster H and gets a direct fix here, and I
  traced *which cand_0001 sentence* caused it rather than guessing. (2) Because Rule 1 clearly landed,
  I followed my own `META_INSIGHTS.md` item 2 and did **not** add more formula prose, and did **not**
  test the item-3 "move the formula ban next to the write step" placement hypothesis — that was
  contingent on Rule 1 *failing*, and it didn't. `rejected.jsonl` is empty, so nothing needed
  structural avoidance.

- **Refuted hypotheses** — none refuted by a RESULT yet beyond cand_0001's two. Refuted by evidence
  *this* iteration, do not re-test: (1) **9569 is not a selection-logic failure** — its rule matches
  gold exactly; the loss is entirely self-inflicted rounding, so writing another filtering rule for it
  is wasted. (2) **560-12's `int where str expected` is not a type bug** — a type-table edit cannot
  fix it; it is geometry. (3) **There is still no environment fault** — all 40 graded consistently.

- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked** — none knowingly: all three failures got a targeted edit
  plus the shared structural fix. What is untested is compliance: whether this reader actually *builds*
  `PLAN` rather than writing code that looks like it. If 59595 still fails with `'n/a'` in C4, the
  answer is not more wording — it is that the agent must print the verdict table before the save, and
  the next lever would be making the save itself refuse (`assert set(PLAN)==set(CELLS)` placed *above*
  `wb.save`, which it already is) or moving the whole PLAN step into `prompt.md` as a hard contract.

- **Plateau signal** — not a plateau: one ACCEPT at +0.575. But the **headroom is now 0.075 and the
  measurement is 3 tasks**, so from here a single regression outweighs fixing all three. That
  asymmetry, not the score, is what drove every design choice above, and it is why I rejected
  mandating a read-only first code block (**16 of 37 passing tasks save in round 1** — UNBOUNDED).
  The lever switched from *adding knowledge* (iteration 1) to *code enforcement of a decision the
  agent already makes implicitly* (this one).

- **Focus next iteration** — read the RESULT's `broke={...}` first and check it against the carve-outs
  named above (2768, 53647, 50768, 6698, 463-17, 80-42, 142-12, 382-10) before touching any of them;
  each one is load-bearing for a specific passing task and the blunt version of its rule regresses
  that task. If the anchor fix landed but 59595 persists, the remaining defect is compliance with
  `PLAN` — consider hoisting it into `prompt.md`. If 9569 persists, print its 9 tie-break rows to see
  whether the agent rounded again or mis-selected. And there is one **known latent wrongness** worth
  spending spare capacity on: Rule 3 says *"never rename, add, remove or reorder sheets"*, but passing
  tasks **395-36** and **402-43** both add a sheet and pass. I skipped it on the REAL test (no failing
  task needs it), but it is a false statement sitting in the prompt and a future failure could hinge
  on it.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.925 Δ=+0.000 · fixed={560-12, 59595, 9569} · broke={402-43, 50768, 80-42} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

> Written at iteration 1, so **no entry below is confirmed by a gate RESULT yet**. Everything marked
> *verified in source* was read out of the scorer/adapter code or a saved trajectory, which is
> stronger than a guess but weaker than a RESULT. Re-read this file after cand_0001 is stamped.

## The grading contract (verified in source — treat as fact, not hypothesis)

- `evaluation.py::compare_workbooks` opens **both** the golden and the produced file with
  `openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)`, and the adapter's `REWARD_RECALC` defaults to
  `"0"`, so the primary metric `hard_no_recalc` **never recalculates**. openpyxl writes a formula
  with no cached `<v>`, so **any formula in a graded cell reads back `None` and scores 0** however
  correct it is. This single fact accounts for 25 of the 26 iteration-1 failures.
- `transform_value` rounds numbers to 2 decimals, converts datetimes to a float day number, and
  coerces numeric-looking strings via `float()`; `compare_cell_value` then requires
  `type(v1) == type(v2)`. `""` and `None` are explicitly equal. Fill/font-colour comparisons are
  **commented out** — only values are graded, so formatting effort is wasted unless the instruction
  asks for it.
- `answer_position` sheet resolution: the part before `!` with `'` stripped from *either* end (real
  data contains lopsided quoting like `worksheet2'!C3:C6`); with **no `!` the graded sheet is
  `wb_gt.sheetnames[0]`, NOT `wb.active`**.
- `instruction_type` is **not** used by the comparator — Cell-Level and Sheet-Level both compare the
  whole `answer_position` range.
- Over the 40 tasks, `answer_position` is 33 rectangles + 7 single cells: **no comma-lists and no
  full-column ranges**, so range-parsing code only needs those two shapes. The largest is
  `'Consolidate_ALL'!A2:L8000` = 95,988 cells, which matters because enumerating it in openpyxl
  auto-vivifies every cell and can blow the 60-second block limit.

## The seed was a no-skill control (verified in source)

An empty `prompt.md` makes `_read_system_prompt` return `""` and **no system message is sent at
all**; a missing `task_template.md` falls back to the adapter's built-in `_TASK_TEMPLATE`, which
contains *"once that file exists, you are done"* and no verification step. Baseline 0.350 is
therefore a floor measured with no guidance, not a tuned starting point — do not read it as
"prompting only buys a little here".

## Passing tasks whose behaviour a plausible rule would break (verified in the passing traces)

These are the landmines. Each one is a *passing* task that depends on the opposite of a rule it is
tempting to write:

- **80-42** passes *because* it writes the literal strings `"None"` (cols D–I) and `"N/A"` (col J)
  into ~7000 graded cells, matching the convention of the existing rows. A blanket "never write a
  filler like `N/A` into a cell whose answer is nothing" is a deterministic regression.
- **382-10** must **clear** `A18`, which holds `=IFERROR(#REF!/#REF!,0)`, to `None` — and the
  instruction never names A18. So "replace a formula with its computed value" and "cells the
  instruction doesn't name keep their original value" are *both* wrong as absolutes.
- **463-17 and 6698** pass by editing the xlsx's XML through `zipfile`, not through openpyxl
  (463-17 only after its openpyxl attempt hit the 60-second limit). "Edit the loaded workbook and
  save it" would regress both.
- **463-17 and 416-15** depend on writing the *original* value, not the normalised key they matched
  on — so scope any normalisation advice to the comparison only.
- **560-12, 6698, 80-42** do explicitly-requested formatting work. "Formatting is not graded" is
  true of the comparator but must not be phrased as "ignore formatting instructions".

## The "#N/A error text" diagnostic is misleading (verified against the saved artifacts)

Six tasks' feedback says the cells contain Excel error text. None of them wrote an `"#N/A"` literal
and none used `data_only=True`. They wrote post-2007 functions **bare** (`AGGREGATE`, `UNIQUE`,
`TEXTJOIN`, `FILTER`, `TEXTSPLIT`, `MAXIFS`); the xlsx grammar requires these as `_xlfn.*`, so the
LibreOffice recalc used to produce the diagnostic resolved them to `#NAME?`/`#VALUE!`. They are
cluster A (formula-instead-of-value), seen through the recalculated copy. **Do not spend an
iteration adding an `_xlfn.` rule** — it only helps an answer that is a formula, which is the losing
strategy on the primary metric.

## Where the ground truth was sitting in the file (pattern, verified in 3 of 4 non-formula failures)

SpreadsheetBench instructions are written by the file's owner, who usually did the first rows by
hand. 59196's `H3` already held the correct `'D'` (the agent overwrote it); 43436's column header
*"Open by of end of May 2022"* plus the user's neighbouring `H2=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")` disambiguate
the prose clause the agent got wrong; 51-12's row 2 held the markers `1,2,3,4`. **A pre-filled cell
inside `answer_position` is free validation of your reading of the instruction** — and
simultaneously a cell you must not overwrite.

## Promising but not yet tried

- Making the Round-3 `changed`-set comparison an **assert** (it is currently a printout the agent has
  to interpret). Same for a declared type expectation. Code enforcement beat prose on the formula
  rule; it should beat prose on the over-write rule too.
- If Rule 1 under-performs, relocating the formula ban from `prompt.md` into `task_template.md` right
  beside the write step — placement next to the action may matter more than wording for this reader.
- A layout/matrix sub-rule for the hardest cluster-B case (9 boxes, 6 of which must stay blank).

---

> Added at iteration 2, after cand_0001 was stamped **ACCEPTED val=0.925 Δ=+0.575,
> fixed={24 tasks}, broke={560-12}**. The items above are now RESULT-confirmed where noted.

## cand_0001's big rule is CONFIRMED (gate RESULT, cand_0001)

- **What worked:** the formula-is-always-`None` rule plus the mandatory Round-3 CHECK fixed **24 of
  26** tasks in one move (val 0.350 → 0.925). The "read the scorer, not the scorer's error messages"
  method is vindicated: the 6 tasks whose feedback blamed *"Excel error text"* were all in the 24
  fixed, exactly as predicted, and **no `_xlfn.` rule was ever needed**. Do not re-open that.
- **What didn't:** the rule's *side text* broke **560-12**. The sentence *"Cells already filled in are
  usually the user's own worked EXAMPLE … leave the example cells as they are"* is a liability — it
  also caused 59595. A "leave what's already there" instruction with no condition attached will be
  read as "those cells are out of scope".
- **Confirmed safe after a full passing-trace audit:** all four at-risk carve-outs held — 80-42
  (literal `"None"`/`"N/A"` across ~7000 cells), 382-10 (must clear A18), 463-17 and 6698 (XML
  surgery). None appears in `broke`. **The carve-outs are load-bearing; do not "simplify" them.**

## The type contract is looser than it looks (verified in source; corrects the iteration-1 entry)

`transform_value` sends `int`, `float` **and** any `float()`-parseable `str` through
`round(float(v), 2)` before `compare_cell_value` checks `type(v1) == type(v2)`. Therefore:

- **`int` vs `float` NEVER matters, and a numeric string equals a number** — `42`, `42.0`, `"42"` are
  one value. Any prompt text asking the agent to normalise integral floats to `int` is pure waste, and
  ~21 passing tasks write `int` happily.
- The type errors that **do** cost cells are exactly two: a string `float()` cannot parse (`'n/a'`,
  `'-'`, `'TBD'`, an error text) sitting where a number is expected, and a number parsed out of text
  where non-numeric text is expected.
- **Corollary that matters more than the type rule itself:** because the grader rounds to 2 dp, any
  self-chosen rounding to 3 or 4 dp can only *create* `x.xx5` tie-breaks that flip the wrong way.
  This is the entire cause of 9569's 1261/1280 wrong cells — its selection rule matched gold exactly.

## `answer_position` is a bounding box and the corner is not the anchor (verified in the traces)

- **10 of 40 tasks have gold-EMPTY cells inside `answer_position`**, and several have padding cells
  holding pre-existing content that must survive. So padding is *"exactly what it arrived as"* —
  never "usually empty".
- **The anchor is set by the instruction, not by the box.** 560-12: *"The answer should be put from
  I3"* with `answer_position` `I2:J7` — gold has I2/J2 empty, headers at I3/J3, data I4:J6.
- **Three addresses that look like anchors and are not** (each one is a real passing task that an
  unqualified anchor rule would break): an address inside a quoted formula or naming source data; a
  **schematic sketch** of column order (**2768** sketches column F while the real destination is
  column H); and the far end of a destination **range** (**53647** is given E7:E16 and gold **E15 is
  empty** — a range fixes only the *start*).

## Measurements that constrain any future edit (verified in the 37 passing traces)

- **16 of the 37 passing tasks do read + write + check in ONE code block** (they save in round 1).
  **Any edit that mandates a read-only first block is therefore UNBOUNDED** and is the single most
  likely way to lose a large chunk of 0.925. I rejected it on the SAFE test; do not re-propose it.
- **6698 passes by overwriting a pre-filled cached figure that was itself WRONG.** So "your answer
  must agree with a figure the sheet already contains" can only ever be *soft corroboration* —
  turning it into an `assert` deterministically breaks 6698.
- **395-36 and 402-43 both ADD a sheet and pass**, so `prompt.md` Rule 3's *"never rename, add,
  remove or reorder sheets"* is literally false. It is harmless today (no failing task needs it) but
  it is a wrong statement sitting in the prompt — fix it in an iteration with spare capacity.

## Promising but not yet tried

- If `PLAN` (cand_0002) lands, the same trick is available one level up: have the agent print the
  **rule** it derived in words in Round 1 and assert the rule reproduces every pre-filled cell. That
  attacks "the plan is complete but wrong", which is the one failure mode `assert not offplan` cannot
  catch by construction.
- Hoisting the `PLAN` requirement from `task_template.md` into `prompt.md` as a contract, if the
  template version is built but not honoured. Placement is still an untested variable on this reader.
- A rule for openpyxl serialising `0.0` as the string `"0"` — observed in 9569 but it has never been
  the deciding defect, so it is not worth an iteration on its own.

## From iteration cand_0003 (attribution of cand_0002's mixed rejection; VERIFIED against traces + scorer source)

**VERIFIED — the grader's 2-dp rounding does not forgive your rounding; it compounds it.**
`transform_value` does `round(float(v), 2)` on **both** sides, which tempts you into thinking an
intermediate round to 3 or 4 decimals is harmless. It is not: your round plus the grader's is
**double rounding**, and it breaks `x.xx5` ties the opposite way. Measured on task 9569 (1280 cells):
rounding to 4 dp first produced **9 wrong cells**, and 9 is as fatal as 1261 under all-or-nothing
range grading. Gold `0.145021572`→`0.15` but `0.145`→`0.14`; `0.075000259`→`0.08` but `0.075`→`0.07`;
`0.034966941`→`0.03` but `0.035`→`0.04`; `0.264999741`→`0.26` but `0.265`→`0.27`. **Rule: assign the
workbook's value object straight through; round only when the instruction asks you to.**

**VERIFIED — a worked example's digit count is not part of the specification.** Spreadsheet owners
type what their number format displays, so a pre-filled cell can hold a rounded transcription of a
source value the sheet stores at full precision — and the **full value** is what the gold answer
holds (9569: gold `AO9 = 0.170687841`, the owner's cell held `0.1707`, confirmed against the golden
workbook). *"Make your rule reproduce the example exactly"* is therefore a trap: it is what drove
cand_0001 to round. Reproduce an example's **rule**, never its digit count — and if your rule only
matches once you round, the rounding is wrong, not the rule.

**VERIFIED — "is this pre-filled cell an example or a placeholder?" is ONE decision class with
OPPOSITE correct answers, and the discriminator is the column, not the cell.** 59595 needs the
pre-filled `'n/a'` **overwritten** (its neighbours `C7:C11` hold real computed integers, so the
marker is the odd one out); 80-42 needs `"None"`/`"N/A"` **preserved** (they are the convention
across ~1000 existing rows). cand_0002 rewrote the class-wide rule and therefore traded one for the
other — it fixed 59595 and broke 80-42, exactly as the diagnose skill predicts for a class-wide
change. **The discriminating condition that separates them: does the marker recur down the rest of
that column (⇒ it is the table's way of writing "no value", keep it), or is it the odd one out among
real computed entries (⇒ it is a placeholder for the value you were asked to compute, overwrite it)?**

**VERIFIED — `answer_position` is a bounding BOX, and the answer's anchor inside it is a separate
question from the box's corner.** Three-step precedence, in order: a cell/row/column the instruction
names **inside** the box wins (560-12: box `I2:J7`, instruction says *"put the answer from I3"*, so
`I2:J2` keeps its original contents); failing that, a place the instruction *describes* ("into the
first available blank rows" — 80-42; "continue under the last entry"); only failing both does the
answer start at the box's top-left. **And the anchor fixes only where the answer STARTS.** Which
value lands in which row and column is fixed by the labels the sheet prints along the box's edges,
plus any orientation the instruction states. 50768 is the proof of the converse: told to print an
anchor conclusion for a 3×3 matrix whose instruction names no address, the agent invented a "matrix
convention" and **transposed the axes, overriding labels it had itself printed**. Never lay out a
grid from convention while the sheet labels its own axes.

**VERIFIED — the `PLAN`/`LEAVE` dict + `assert not offplan` apparatus does not work on this
benchmark, and the reason is specific enough to generalize.** It was vacuous on all three tasks it
was built for (59595's fix appeared in the agent's **first** code block, before `PLAN` existed), and
it was actively harmful twice: on 9569 `assert not offplan` fired on openpyxl float round-tripping
(`('AO79','0.373369645','0.37336964500000003')`) and cost a round — and note its natural "fix" is to
round, the one thing that loses that task; on 80-42 the added machinery coincided with the agent
collapsing into a single silent code block with no exploration round at all. **An assert over
floating-point cell values has a false-positive rate that an agent pays for in rounds, and the
cheapest way for it to silence that assert is the behaviour you most need to forbid.**

**REFUTED, do not re-test:** (a) cand_0001's `number_format = "0.00%"` overwrite is **not** why 9569
lost — colour/fill/font comparison in `evaluation.py` is **commented out** (lines 140–151) and only
`compare_cell_value` runs, so no formatting is ever compared; (b) **int-vs-float can never decide a
cell**, so the harness feedback *"hold int where float was expected — match the expected type
exactly"* is a pre-normalisation diagnostic and is **misleading** — both go through
`round(float(v), 2)`. The type check only ever bites a string that `float()` cannot parse (`n/a`,
`-`, `TBD`), which type-mismatches any number and scores 0.

**Still-known-false statements left in `prompt.md` on purpose** (both fail the REAL test today — no
task fails because of them — so they are pruning work for an iteration with headroom, not fixes):
*"never rename, add, remove or reorder sheets"* (passing tasks **395-36** and **402-43** both add a
sheet) and the Rule 2 table row claiming the text `"42"` never works where a number is expected (the
scorer parses numeric-looking strings, so it does work; writing a real number is still better advice).

## From iteration cand_0004 — the pre-filled-cell cluster, third attempt (VERIFIED against the golden workbook)

**VERIFIED — "does the marker recur down the column?" is NOT a usable discriminator, and the RESULT
proves it.** `cand_0003` shipped exactly that condition and its RESULT is `fixed={560-12, 9569}` — 59595
untouched. The trace shows why: the marker `'n/a'` occupies **C4, C5 and C6**, so *"if the same marker
recurs in the other rows … you keep it"* was satisfied on its own terms and selected the wrong branch.
A frequency test over the column cannot separate 59595 from 80-42. Do not re-propose it in any wording.

**VERIFIED — the discriminator that gold actually encodes is the INSTRUCTION'S SCOPE.** Read out of
`1_59595_golden.xlsx` (sheet XML via `zipfile`; openpyxl is not installed in the optimizer shell):
gold `C4=4, C5=6, C6=12 … C19=34`, and the owner's own formula is a **shared formula with
`ref="C4:C19"`** — one rule applied uniformly to all 16 rows, including the three `'n/a'` rows. Gold
tracks what the instruction's rule covers, never which cells arrived filled. The four keep-reasons that
make this safe across the suite: (1) the instruction scopes the work to the *blank/new/remaining* rows
(80-42: *"into the first available, blank rows"*); (2) the rule is **conditional** and its condition is
false there (142-12: *"Whenever these conditions are met…"*); (3) the rule only **reads** that cell —
a key, a criterion, an amount compared (142-12's `G:J`); (4) the rule's value is *nothing* (53647's
gold-empty `E15`).

**VERIFIED — the failure was a RETREAT after a clean save, and the check's own wording caused it.**
59595 wrote the gold values in round 2 (`16 checked | 16 non-empty | 11 changed`), then wrote
`# Keep the sheet's established convention…` + `ws[f"C{r}"] = wsv[f"C{r}"].value` and shipped
`8 changed`. The clause responsible was `task_template.md` Round-3 point 3: *"If it is larger, you have
overwritten cells whose expected value was their own original content."* **A size test on `changed` is
not a correctness test** — audited over all 40 traces, exactly one task's `changed` decreases between
rounds and it is the failing one; every passing task with a huge `changed` (80-42 47975, 48921 4448,
9569 1280, 395-36 300) saved once and passed. The other half of the clause is false too: **37378**
passes with `changed: ['A4']`, 1 of 5 in-scope cells, because `A2`/`A3` already held the rule's output.
**Absence from `changed` is agreement, not omission.** General lesson worth more than the fix: ask
*which instruction the agent was acting on at the moment it went wrong* — three iterations edited the
policy prose while the defect lived in the verification step.

**VERIFIED — 80-42 was never protected by the marker rule.** Its trace finds `start_row = 4000` by
scanning for the first all-blank row and copies source values through verbatim
(`vals = [sws_v.cell(sr, c).value for c in src_cols]`); the recurring `'N/A'` in column J is incidental
and no agent reasoning references the marker heuristic. Its **append logic** is the protection. Corollary
for anyone re-reading `cand_0002`'s `broke={80-42}`: what broke it was banning reasoning from emptiness,
because …[+1211 chars truncated]

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001

- **Strategy tried, and whether it moved val:** cannot cite a LEDGER row — this is iteration 1 and
  the ledger is empty. The strategy was: (a) cluster all 26 failures before writing a single word,
  (b) derive every contract claim from the **scorer and adapter source** rather than from the
  feedback strings, (c) run a **passing-trace regression audit** of each drafted rule *before*
  committing it, and (d) prefer one piece of code enforcement over more prose. Outcome unknown until
  the RESULT lands; what is certain is that (b) and (c) each changed the candidate materially.
- **What (b) bought:** the feedback string for 6 of the 26 tasks points at the wrong cause ("Excel
  error text") and would have sent me to write an `_xlfn.` rule — i.e. a rule that helps formulas
  survive, in a benchmark where formulas cannot survive. Reading `evaluation.py` and `adapter.py`
  instead gave the real contract (`data_only=True`, no recalc, `type()` equality,
  `sheetnames[0]`) and collapsed a 3-cluster picture into one 25-task cluster. **Generalizable
  lesson: read the scorer, not the scorer's error messages.**
- **What (c) bought:** three of my drafted rules were deterministic regressions on *passing* tasks
  (80-42, 382-10, 463-17/6698) and a fourth was a timeout risk I introduced myself (my verification
  snippet walked a 95,988-cell range on a passing task). All four were found by auditing the 14
  passing traces against the draft, none by re-reading the failing ones. **Generalizable lesson: the
  failing traces tell you what to add; only the passing traces tell you what it will cost. Budget a
  full pass on them, and treat your own verification code as an edit with a blast radius.**
- **Plateau/stall signal:** none yet. The one stall *within* the iteration was diagnostic: I spent
  effort on two wrong hypotheses for the `#N/A` cluster before delegating it. Fanning out 3 read-only
  subagents (mechanism / non-formula root causes / regression audit) in parallel resolved all three
  questions faster than serial investigation, and the audit was the highest-value of the three.
- **Verification limit to plan around:** `openpyxl` is not installed in the optimizer environment and
  `pip` is unavailable, so I could not execute the snippet I ship. Substitute that worked: enumerate
  the real `answer_position` shapes from the trajectories (33 rects + 7 single cells, no comma-lists,
  no full columns) to learn exactly which branches must work, then test the logic against a faithful
  `Worksheet.__getitem__` stub. That caught the single-cell branch and the 95,988-cell blow-up.
  **Do this before shipping any code block to the agent** — a snippet that raises costs a round, and
  one that times out can lose a passing task.
- **What to try next iteration:**
  1. Read the RESULT and `broke={...}` first; check it against the four at-risk passing tasks named
     in `INSIGHTS.md` before touching any carve-out.
  2. If the big rule landed, **do not add more prose** — convert the Round-3 printouts that the agent
     has to *interpret* (the `changed` set, the types) into asserts. Code enforcement is the lever
     that this reader tier responds to, and it is only half-used so far.
  3. If the big rule did not land, the problem is compliance rather than knowledge: test **placement**
     (formula ban in `task_template.md` next to the write step) as a distinct hypothesis from wording.
     Treat that as a one-variable experiment so the RESULT is attributable.
  4. Keep the iteration-1 move single-lever where possible from now on. This one necessarily changed
     everything at once (empty seed), which means a negative RESULT will be hard to attribute — the
     per-edit blast-radius notes in `PROCESS.md` are the only way back to attribution, so keep them.

## Iteration cand_0002

- **Strategy tried:** the search regime changed shape, and recognising that was the main decision.
  Iteration 1 was *breadth under ignorance* — 26 failures, an empty capability, one huge move.
  Iteration 2 is *precision under asymmetry*: LEDGER row `cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.925 Δ=+0.575,
  fixed={24}, broke={560-12}` leaves **3 failures and +0.075 of headroom against a 2·SE bar on 40
  tasks**. One regression now costs more than fixing all three remaining tasks gains. So I inverted
  the iteration-1 budget: instead of clustering-then-auditing, I ran **root-cause on all 3 failures
  and two passing-trace regression audits in parallel from the start**, and treated every candidate
  rule as guilty until a named carve-out acquitted it. Four carve-outs survived that process (2768,
  53647, 50768, 6698); two whole ideas did not.
- **The lever that iteration 1 pointed at was the right one.** `META_INSIGHTS` item 2 said: if the big
  rule lands, don't add prose — convert the Round-3 printouts the agent has to *interpret* into
  asserts. It landed, and the diagnosis independently arrived at the same place: all three remaining
  failures **ran the check and passed it**, because the agent supplied both the answer and the
  standard. Writing the intent down *before* the save (`PLAN`) and asserting the file against it is
  the only structural way to break that circularity. **Generalizable lesson: when a failing trace
  shows the agent self-certifying, the missing thing is not a rule — it is a record the check can
  disagree with.**
- **What the 'ship breadth' mandate actually bought at 3 failures:** less than it did at 26. Three of
  the nine edits (the verdict table, `PLAN`, `assert not offplan`) carry nearly all the expected
  value; the rest are small knowledge/wording fixes riding along. The honest read is that **breadth
  and safety trade off directly once the failure set is small** — every extra edit is another chance
  to regress 37 tasks for at most 0.025 of upside. I kept the small edits only because each one is
  provably non-action-changing on passing tasks (a removed obligation, a softened claim, a corrected
  fact), not because breadth was asked for.
- **A failure mode of my own prose, found by tracing:** 59595 was caused by a sentence *I wrote in
  cand_0001* — *"Cells already filled in are usually the user's own worked EXAMPLE … leave the
  example cells as they are."* A "leave what's there" instruction with **no discriminating condition**
  reads as "those cells are out of scope". This is the DECISION/PERMISSION lever from the guidance,
  applied to my own text: the fix was not to delete the advice but to attach the condition (a 5-row
  verdict table). **Lesson: audit your own previous iteration's prose as a suspect, not as a given —
  `broke={}` and the surviving failures both point at it.**
- **Verification limit, handled as prescribed and worth keeping:** openpyxl still isn't installed and
  pip is still unavailable. The stub route from iteration 1 worked again and caught real things: I ran
  all three shipped snippets against a faithful `Worksheet.__getitem__`/`range_boundaries` stub over
  six shapes, including two **negative** controls — the `""`↔`None` round-trip (the assert must *not*
  fire; it doesn't) and a deliberately skipped cell (it *must* fire; it does). **Adding negative
  controls is the upgrade over iteration 1** — "it doesn't crash" is not evidence an assert has
  discriminating power, and an assert without discriminating power is a passing-task hazard for free.
- **Plateau signal:** none in the score (one ACCEPT at +0.575), but the *information* rate has
  collapsed — 3 tasks is a very noisy signal against a 2·SE bar, so the next RESULT may be
  unattributable even if the edits are right. Mitigation: `PROCESS.md` records a per-edit blast-radius
  class with named passing tasks, so a `broke={}` set can be mapped back to a specific edit.
- **What to try next iteration:**
  1. Read `broke={...}` and check it against the eight named carve-out tasks (2768, 53647, 50768,
     6698, 463-17, 80-42, 142-12, 382-10) **before** editing any rule that mentions them.
  2. **With only 3 tasks in play, prefer ONE change over many.** The marginal edit now has negative
     expected value unless it is provably non-action-changing. If this candidate is rejected, the
     right response is to re-propose the `PLAN` machinery *alone*, stripped of the four small prose
     edits, so the RESULT is attributable.
  3. If `PLAN` is built but not honoured, the open variable is **placement** (template vs
     `prompt.md`), still untested on this reader after two iterations.
  4. Spend spare capacity on the one known-false statement in the prompt (*"never add sheets"*, which
     passing tasks 395-36 and 402-43 both violate). It fails the REAL test today, so it is explicitly
     a *spare-capacity* item, not a fix.

## Iteration cand_0003

- **Strategy tried, and whether it moved val:** cannot cite my own LEDGER row yet, but the strategy
  was chosen *because of* one: `cand_0002: REJECTED val=0.925 Δ=+0.000, fixed={560-12, 59595, 9569},
  broke={402-43, 50768, 80-42}`. A batch that fixes 3 and breaks 3 is the single most informative
  rejection shape available, and the right response is **not** to re-propose a subset by intuition —
  it is to spend the iteration on **1:1 attribution** (which sentence moved which task) and let the
  edit fall out mechanically. I ran six read-only subagents, one per moved task, and the attribution
  came back clean on all six. That is now the run's most valuable artifact.
- **The generalizable method: a rejected batch is a natural experiment, and the framework hands you
  the instrumentation.** `rollouts/val/` contains the *post-edit* traces of the rejected candidate, so
  for every task that moved you can read what the agent did **under the new text**. That turns
  "3 fixed, 3 broken, net zero" from a dead end into six independent, individually-attributable
  observations. **Do this before proposing anything after a mixed rejection** — it is strictly more
  informative than re-reading the failing tasks, and it is the only way to separate fixing text from
  breaking text that shipped as one batch.
- **The decisive attribution trick: check WHEN in the trajectory the behaviour appeared.** 59595's fix
  showed up in the agent's **first** code block (`if 4 <= r <= 19`), before any output file existed —
  which proves the Round-2 `PLAN` machinery, which had not run yet, cannot have caused it. One
  timestamp argument retired a whole apparatus that three other observations had only made look
  suspicious. **Temporal position inside the trace is evidence that prose comparison cannot give you.**
- **What the attribution overturned, including my own prior note.** `META_INSIGHTS` for cand_0002 said:
  if rejected, re-propose the `PLAN` machinery *alone*, stripped of the small prose edits. The traces
  say the opposite — `PLAN` was **vacuous on all three fixes** and the small prose edits carried them
  all. So I dropped `PLAN` and shipped the prose with narrowing conditions. **Lesson: a
  `what-to-try-next` note is written before the evidence exists; when the evidence arrives, let it
  overrule the note, and say so explicitly rather than honouring the plan.**
- **The real lesson about the DECISION/PERMISSION lever, learned the expensive way.** 59595 and 80-42
  are the *same* decision ("is this pre-filled cell an example or a placeholder?") with **opposite**
  correct answers. cand_0002 rewrote the class-wide rule and therefore could not avoid trading one for
  the other — fixing 59595 *necessarily* broke 80-42. The diagnose skill says this in advance ("fix the
  exact discriminating condition, never the class-wide rule") and cand_0002's own PROCESS.md quoted it;
  it still shipped the class-wide rewrite. **Generalizable: when two tasks in one decision class need
  opposite actions, no amount of rule *strength* helps — the edit must be a condition that separates
  them, and if you cannot name that condition from the data, you do not yet have the edit.** Here the
  condition was findable and cheap: *does the marker recur down the column, or is it the odd one out?*
- **A sampling error I made, and the guard against it.** I spent real effort convinced cand_0002's
  9569 rationale was refuted by the scorer source, because `transform_value` rounds **both** sides to
  2 dp and the first ~10 rows of the range agree under either rounding. The losing rows were at 39,
  49, 310, 574, 578, 592, 630, 893, 1077 — 9 `x.xx5` ties out of 1280. **Guard: on an all-or-nothing
  range metric, never refute a mechanism from a sample; compute the comparison over the whole range,
  which for a 1280-cell range costs one subagent and seconds.** More generally: a normalisation that
  collapses *most* differences does not collapse all of them, and 9 fatal cells are invisible to
  eyeballing while being exactly as fatal as 1261.
- **Verification limit, unchanged and still handled the same way:** `openpyxl` is absent from the
  optimizer environment and `pip` is unavailable, so shipped snippets cannot be executed here. This
  iteration needed less of that than the last two because **I changed no code block** — all three
  edits are prose. That is itself a finding: *prose-only edits are cheaper to verify in this
  environment than snippet edits*, and with a 0.0124 bar and 3 tasks, cheap-to-verify is worth a lot.
- **Plateau signal:** score is flat (+0.575, then +0.000) but this is **not** an information plateau —
  the flat iteration produced the attribution that made this one possible. The honest risk is
  different: at 37/40 passing, the *measurement* is the bottleneck, not the ideas. Three tasks against
  a 2·SE bar means a correct candidate can still land unattributable.
- **What to try next iteration:**
  1. **Read `broke={...}` against the per-edit carve-out lists in `PROCESS.md` first** (50768, 2768,
     53647, 80-42, 382-10, 142-12, 38462). Each edit names the passing tasks it was shaped around, so
     a regression maps straight back to one of three edits instead of a whole batch. This is the
     payoff of keeping the candidate to three independently-attributable edits.
  2. **If all three target tasks moved, stop adding and start pruning.** `prompt.md` has gone
     8585 → 11973 chars across three iterations. Two statements are known-false and are the natural
     prune targets: *"never rename, add, remove or reorder sheets"* (passing tasks 395-36 and 402-43
     both add a sheet) and the Rule 2 table row claiming the text `"42"` never works for a number.
     Both fail the REAL test today, which is exactly why they are *pruning* work for an iteration with
     headroom rather than fixes.
  3. **If a discrimination edit fails again, switch from condition-stating to evidence-printing.**
     The untested lever on this reader is making the agent *print the column's value distribution*
     beside each pre-filled cell in Round 1, so the discriminating fact is on screen when the decision
     is made. That is strictly weaker than an assert — and cand_0002 established that asserts on this
     benchmark regress passing tasks (float noise, over-wide ranges), so weaker is the point.
  4. **Do not spend another iteration on structural machinery in Round 2.** Two iterations of evidence
     now: the `PLAN`/`LEAVE`/`offplan` apparatus was vacuous where it was supposed to help and harmful
     where it was not. The levers that have actually moved tasks on this benchmark are (a) a stated
     mechanism the agent lacked, and (b) a narrowing condition on a decision it was already making.

## Iteration 4 — the search-process lesson: ask WHICH instruction the agent was obeying when it went wrong

- **What helped most, by a wide margin:** re-reading the failing trace for **when** the wrong value
  appeared, not just **what** was wrong. 59595 had been read three times as "the agent preserves a
  marker it should overwrite", and all three iterations therefore edited the *policy* prose in
  `prompt.md` Rule 3. The trace actually shows the agent writing the **gold** answer in round 2, the
  check printing clean, and the agent then *undoing it* — acting on `task_template.md`'s Round-3
  point 3 (*"If it is larger, you have overwritten cells…"*), a sentence in a different file and a
  different section from everything three iterations had been editing. **Generalised heuristic: for
  any behavioural failure, locate the turn where the trajectory diverges and read the instruction that
  governs THAT turn.** A policy rule and a verification rule can disagree, and the verification rule
  wins because it runs last.
- **Meta-lesson about this benchmark's prompt surface:** the two editable files are not "system prompt"
  and "framing". `prompt.md` is the *policy*; `task_template.md` contains the *procedure and the
  checks*, and the checks are what the agent acts on immediately before finishing. An iteration that
  only edits `prompt.md` can be defeated by a check sentence that tells the agent to undo the policy.
  Grep both files for text governing the same decision before editing either.
- **A size test is not a correctness test, and it had a second false alarm nobody had noticed.** The
  removed clause's other half (*"if it is smaller, you have skipped cells you were asked to fill"*) is
  false on passing task 37378 (`changed: ['A4']`, 1 of 5 in-scope cells, because two already held the
  rule's output). It survived three iterations because the task passes anyway. **When you delete a
  clause for one failure, check its other half against the passing set — you may be fixing two bugs.**
- **What worked procedurally:** three parallel read-only subagents, each with ONE narrow question and
  an explicit "quote verbatim, recommend nothing" instruction. The highest-value output was not the
  confirmation I expected but a landmine I had not considered: the preserved-cell audit found that
  **142-12**'s rule is *conditional* and its loop nominally covers every row, so the scope rule I was
  about to write would have overwritten 43 cells and lost the task. Keep-reasons 2 and 3 exist because
  an audit ran **before** the edit was written, not after. **Audit the blast radius before drafting,
  not to validate a draft** — drafting first biases you toward confirming your wording.
- **What stalled / was retired:** condition-stating on marker *frequency* (`cand_0003`) is now refuted
  by a RESULT, joining class-wide flips (`cand_0002`) and asserts over cell values. Three of the four
  designs for this one cluster are dead. The remaining untried lever is **evidence-printing** — have
  Round 1 print, per in-range cell, `in-scope` / `out-of-scope: <reason>` before any write, so a
  retreat has to contradict the agent's own printout. I did not take it this iteration because the
  retreat had a simpler, documented cause worth removing first, and stacking both would have made the
  result unattributable.
- **On restraint at 39/40:** I skipped the two known-false statements again, for the third iteration
  running. At one failing task and a 0.0124 bar, the value of a *clean, single-cluster, attributable*
  diff exceeds the value of cosmetic correctness with no measurable effect. If iteration 5 inherits a
  1.000 val, that is the iteration to prune in — with nothing else in the diff.
- **Standing advice for iteration 5:** check `broke={...}` against **142-12** (conditional rule,
  read-only columns) and **80-42** (blank-row scop …[+107 chars truncated]

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From cand_0001 (spreadsheetbench, empty seed)

1. **The optimizer environment lacks the library the capability is about.** `openpyxl` is not
   installed and `pip` is unavailable, so I could not execute the verification snippet I was shipping
   into `task_template.md` — and that snippet is code the agent will run under a 60-second limit on
   40 tasks, including passing ones. I substituted a hand-written `Worksheet.__getitem__` stub, which
   did catch two real defects (a single-cell range branch, and a 95,988-cell enumeration that would
   have risked a timeout on a *passing* task), but a stub is not a test. **Suggestion:** give the
   proposer a read-only scratch venv containing the benchmark's own runtime dependencies (or just
   permit `pip install --user` into a throwaway dir), so code destined for the agent can be executed
   once before it ships. This is cheap and strictly reduces wasted iterations.

2. **Per-task feedback strings can point away from the real cause, and there is no way to flag that.**
   Six of my 26 failures were reported as *"the answer cells contain Excel error text (e.g. #N/A)"*.
   That description is produced from a **recalculated** copy of the file, while the primary metric
   (`hard_no_recalc`) never recalculates. The actual defect in all six was the same as in the other
   19 — a formula where a literal value was needed — and the error text was an artifact of
   LibreOffice resolving bare post-2007 function names (`UNIQUE`, `TEXTJOIN`, …) that the xlsx grammar
   requires as `_xlfn.*`. Taken at face value, the message leads a proposer to spend an iteration
   making formulas *recalculate better*, which cannot help the metric being optimized.
   **Suggestion:** label which metric each feedback line was computed under (e.g. prefix
   `[recalc-diagnostic]` vs `[primary]`), or suppress recalc-derived diagnostics when
   `REWARD_RECALC=0`. The information is useful, but it needs its provenance attached.

3. **Nothing in the brief says whether the seed is an empty *control* or a tuned starting point, and
   the difference changes the whole strategy.** I had to read `adapter.py` to learn that an empty
   `prompt.md` means *no system message is sent at all* and a missing `task_template.md` falls back to
   a built-in template — which, in this case, contained the single most harmful line in the baseline
   ("once that file exists, you are done"). Until I found that, the 0.350 baseline looked like
   evidence that prompting buys little here. **Suggestion:** when a capability file is empty or
   absent, state in the iteration brief what the harness substitutes, and include the substituted
   text. Otherwise iteration 1 is partly spent rediscovering the control condition.

4. **The "VERIFIED" test asks for a trace quote, but a trace quote is often the weakest available
   evidence.** My strongest verifications came from reading the scorer and the adapter (which proved
   *why* the cells read back empty) and from auditing the 14 *passing* traces (which is what caught
   three regressions). The failing traces only showed the symptom. **Suggestion:** make the
   passing-trace blast-radius audit an explicit, named step in the brief's checklist rather than
   something a proposer has to invent — and allow source citations to satisfy VERIFIED on equal
   footing with trace lines. One sentence in the brief would have saved me a near-miss on 80-42.

## From cand_0002 (spreadsheetbench, 3 failures left of 40)

5. **The "ship as many fixes as possible" mandate is correct early and actively harmful late, and the
   brief does not scale it.** At iteration 1 I had 26 failures and breadth was obviously right. At
   iteration 2 I have **3 failures and +0.075 of headroom against a 2·SE significance bar**, so each
   additional edit risks 37 passing tasks for at most 0.025 of upside, and a multi-edit candidate makes
   a `broke={...}` result nearly unattributable. The brief's wording ("breadth is the goal; the only
   brake is regression") pushed the same direction in both regimes. **Suggestion:** make the breadth
   instruction a function of the remaining failure count — e.g. above ~20% failing, ask for breadth;
   below ~10%, ask for *one* structurally-isolated change plus an explicit attributability argument.
   The framework knows the failure count when it writes the brief, so this is free.

6. **There is no way to propose a two-candidate A/B within one iteration, which is what a small failure
   set actually needs.** My three remaining failures have two independent causes (geometry/anchoring,
   and self-certification of a wrong plan). Shipping both means one RESULT for two hypotheses. Shipping
   one wastes an iteration out of five. **Suggestion:** let an iteration emit two sibling candidates
   scored against the same champion, with the budget counting it as one iteration if both are cheap.
   Attribution is the scarce resource at this stage, not compute.

7. **`unresolved={—}` is reported but its threshold is not.** The brief warns that unresolved tasks
   "moved less than 2·SE of their own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks", which
   is exactly the right caution, but I cannot tell how close a task came to that bar. A task that moved
   1.9·SE and one that did not move at all are very different signals for designing the next edit.
   **Suggestion:** report the per-task delta and its SE alongside the verdict, or at least bucket them
   (`moved-but-insignificant` vs `flat`).

8. **Negative controls should be part of the VERIFIED test when the edit ships code.** Iteration 1's
   advice (test your snippet against a stub before shipping) was good but incomplete: this iteration I
   added two *negative* controls — one input where a new `assert` must NOT fire (the `""`↔`None`
   round-trip) and one where it MUST (a deliberately skipped cell). "It doesn't crash" is not evidence
   that an assert discriminates, and a non-discriminating assert is a pure downside risk on passing
   tasks. **Suggestion:** when a candidate adds an assertion to agent-facing code, require both
   directions in the PROCESS write-up.

## From iteration cand_0003

- **`prior_iterations/<id>/diff.patch` is truncated, which breaks the one workflow the file exists
  for.** `prior_iterations/cand_0002/diff.patch` ends with a literal `... (truncated)` at line 112 and
  the **entire `task_template.md` half of the diff is absent**. Since `task_template.md` is ~60% of the
  words the agent reads, that is most of the prior iteration's edit missing from the artifact whose
  stated purpose is "read the ones targeting your cluster BEFORE proposing, so you build on prior work
  instead of repeating it". I recovered it with `diff -u candidates/cand_0001/* candidates/cand_0002/*`,
  which works only because `candidates/<id>/` happens to retain full copies. **Suggested fix:** do not
  truncate `diff.patch` at all (these are two text files — the full diff is a few KB), or if a cap is
  needed, truncate **per-file** so every edited file is represented, and say in `CLAUDE.md` that
  `candidates/<id>/` holds the authoritative full text.
- **The gate's feedback string contains a diagnostic that is actively misleading, and a candidate can
  be built on it.** `TYPE: N cell(s) hold int where float was expected — match the expected type
  exactly` is computed **before** the scorer's own normalisation, and `transform_value` sends both
  `int` and `float` through `round(float(v), 2)`, so int-vs-float can *never* decide a cell. Two
  iterations in a row I had to go read `evaluation.py` to discover the message was wrong. **Suggested
  fix:** compute the TYPE line post-`transform_value`, so it only reports type mismatches that
  actually scored 0 (in practice: a string `float()` cannot parse, sitting where a number is expected).
  That one change would have saved real iteration budget both times.
- **Consider surfacing a per-task `fixed`/`broke` attribution hint when a candidate's RESULT is mixed.**
  `fixed={3} broke={3} Δ=+0.000` is the most informative rejection shape there is, but extracting it
  cost this iteration six subagents reading post-edit traces by hand. The framework already copies the
  rejected candidate's trajectories into `rollouts/val/`, which is what made the attribution possible —
  that is a genuinely good design choice and worth keeping. A cheap addition: for each task in
  `broke={...}`/`fixed={...}`, record the first trajectory **turn index** at which the new behaviour
  appears. Temporal position inside the trace is what let me prove the Round-2 `PLAN` machinery could
  not have caused 59595's fix (the behaviour appeared in the agent's *first* block), and it is
  mechanical to compute.

## From iteration 4

- **The optimizer shell has no `openpyxl`, on a benchmark whose every artifact is an `.xlsx`.** Reading
  the golden workbook is the single highest-value verification step available here — it is what turned
  *"the discarded round-2 output would probably have passed"* into proof this iteration, and what
  refuted two earlier hypotheses in `cand_0003`. Doing it requires hand-parsing
  `xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml` + `xl/sharedStrings.xml` through `zipfile`, which costs a tool round and is
  easy to get wrong (shared formulas, the shared-string table, serial dates). **Suggested fix:** install
  `openpyxl` in the optimizer environment, or ship a tiny read-only `dump_xlsx.py` helper in
  `guidance/`. Note the *agent* environment has openpyxl; only the *optimizer's* does not, which is a
  surprising asymmetry given the optimizer is the one told to "read the answer/expected artifact".
- **`INSTRUCTIONS.md` pushes hard for breadth ("ship AS MANY real fixes as you can") in a run state
  where breadth is unavailable and actively risky.** At 39/40 passing with a 0.2·SE bar, there is one
  failing cluster, and every additional edit is by definition aimed at a non-failing task — which the
  same document correctly forbids under the REAL test. The two instructions pull in opposite
  directions, and resolving it took real reasoning time in three consecutive iterations. **Suggested
  fix:** scale the breadth language to the measured state — when the framework knows there is 1 failing
  task, say so ("one cluster remains; depth and attributability matter more than breadth") instead of
  emitting the same "a timid one- or two-edit iteration is an under-used iteration" text.
- **The `## (a) ALWAYS-failing` summary block is truncated mid-sentence** (`TYP`), cutting off exactly
  the TYPE diagnostic line that names the defect. The full string is available in the trajectory's
  `score.feedback`, so no information is lost — but the truncated block is the first thing the
  optimizer reads, and a reader who trusted it would have the key fact amputated. Truncate on a
  sentence boundary, or raise the limit for the single-failing-task case.
